sections.h2: A city split between two counties
sections.html:
Hattiesburg is the seat of Forrest County and the center of the Pine Belt in south Mississippi. Most of the city lies in Forrest County, and a smaller western portion, much of it commercial land added in a 2008 annexation, lies in Lamar County. The 2020 count was 48,730 residents.

Why it matters: your tax collector, tax assessor and chancery clerk all depend on which county holds your parcel. Confirm the county first, before you ask a title company to prorate taxes or record a deed.

Demand comes from several directions: the University of Southern Mississippi, William Carey University, health care, manufacturing and Camp Shelby south of the city. Student housing and rentals are part of the market, and some sellers are landlords ready to stop managing a rental. If that is you, check lease status and deposits before you sell. A written record of the lease terms helps a buyer and keeps the closing simple.

Hattiesburg grew around the railroads, and it has a historic core and a long list of older streets. The city has a Historic Conservation Commission and a design guidelines manual for historic districts, so a house in one of those districts may need a Certificate of Appropriateness before exterior work. Ask the city's planning office at 601-545-4599 whether your address is covered.

Before you list an older house, walk it with a critical eye and decide what you will fix, what you will disclose and what you will leave for the buyer. Fixes that need a permit should be permitted, and receipts should be kept. Older homes bring familiar repair items: original wiring, galvanized or cast iron plumbing and settled foundations. A buyer's lender may balk at these. An investor buying for cash usually does not.

Spring thunderstorms here can bring heavy rain, large hail and tornadoes. An EF4 tornado on February 10, 2013 formed in Lamar County and moved east into Hattiesburg, causing EF1 to EF3 damage near the University of Southern Mississippi campus and in neighborhoods just north of downtown. An EF3 tornado struck early on January 21, 2017.

Seller-side effects of that history include these:

  • Buyers and insurers ask about roof age and any storm repairs.
  • Insurance claim files, contractor invoices and permits should stay with the house paperwork.
  • Damage left unrepaired is a disclosure item and affects what a traditional buyer's lender will finance.

sections.h2: Permits, code rules and the Home Warranty Act
sections.html:
A permit is generally required to build, repair or alter a residence, though some routine repairs may not need one. The Urban Development Department handles planning, zoning, permits, building inspections and code enforcement from City Hall at 200 Forrest Street. The building division number is 601-554-1003, and code enforcement is 601-554-1027.

Zoning follows the city's Land Development Code, and the building code is the 2018 International Residential Code. Permitted work must be inspected before it is covered, and the city asks for at least 24 hours of notice for an inspection.

One item deserves a seller's attention. The city's residential page says an owner who acts as his or her own contractor on a single-family home may be subject to the Mississippi Home Warranty Act and, if the home is later sold, may be required to warrant it for up to seven years from the sale date. If you built or added to your home yourself, talk with an attorney before you sell.

The city also publishes floodplain information. If your property is near the Leaf or Bouie rivers, ask about its flood designation.

Taxes in both counties are due by February 1. The Forrest County Tax Collector is at 601 N. Main Street in downtown Hattiesburg, and Lamar County gives February 1 as the last day to pay without interest.

Here is how Forrest County's process runs: the tax assessor appraises property, the board of supervisors reviews the rolls after a protest period, and the collector applies the assessment ratios and the levy set by the board and the City of Hattiesburg. After you buy a property, it can take up to a year for the new deed to show on the tax map, because the mapper works from the previous year's recorded deeds.

Lamar County adds a $3 publication fee on August 1 for advertising a lien. If your address is on the west side, find out which county bills you before the title company prorates the taxes.

The quickest routes skip the listing process. A cash sale to an investor can close in a short time because there is no lender appraisal, and it lets you leave behind repairs, storm damage or a tenant situation that would complicate a retail sale.

Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523 of the Mississippi Code ask sellers of covered homes to give the buyer a written statement of the property's condition before title passes. Gather what you know about the roof, plumbing, wiring and past claims either way. Whichever county your parcel sits in, that county's chancery clerk records the deed.

Here is the order most Hattiesburg sales follow:

  1. Confirm the county of your parcel, Forrest or Lamar.
  2. Ask that county's tax collector what is owed and when each bill is due.
  3. Check with the Urban Development Department for open permits or code notices.
  4. Collect storm repair, insurance and contractor records.
  5. Sign a purchase contract, let a title company search and clear the title, then close and record the deed.

Landlords selling near the universities should add the lease, rent roll and deposit records to the pile. Heirs should add the estate paperwork, since a title company will need to see who has authority to sign. None of this is hard to collect, but missing pieces are what usually push a closing past its date.

Whatever route you choose, compare net proceeds. On paper a listing can show a bigger figure, yet agent commissions, repairs, carrying costs and months of waiting are all subtracted from it. An offer from us is not a promise of a price, and you can decline it.

faqs.a: Most of Hattiesburg is in Forrest County, which is the county seat. A western portion of the city is in Lamar County, so confirm the county for your parcel.

faqs.q: When are Forrest County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By February 1 each year. The Tax Collector's office is at 601 N. Main Street in Hattiesburg and takes payments online as well.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair my Hattiesburg house before selling?
faqs.a: Generally yes, to repair or alter an existing residence, though certain routine repairs may not need one. Call the building division at 601-554-1003 before starting work.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hattiesburg house that was damaged by a tornado?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell it as is, but disclose known damage and keep insurance and repair records. Cash buyers often take storm-damaged houses that lenders will not finance.

faqs.q: What is the Mississippi Home Warranty Act issue for owner-built homes?
faqs.a: The city says an owner who acts as his or her own contractor may be required to warrant the home for up to seven years from the sale date. Ask an attorney how that applies to your house.
